results.corrected_extracted: Systematic review of clinical trials of classic psychedelics for psychiatric disorders, excluding treatment for substance use disorders: PubMed and Web of Science searched to 12 September 2022 and rerun on 6 December 2023, with English- or French-language publications eligible. It reports 27 articles grouped into 25 studies, classified as 13 randomized and 12 open-label; Table 1 has 25 study rows, comprising 16 psilocybin, five ayahuasca, two LSD and two labelled DMT. The Results reports 761 participants, and the Table 1 row totals independently sum to 761; the abstract instead reports 763. These are the review's study entries and participant totals, not independently verified counts of distinct trials or people from the primary reports. No review protocol, registration or formal trial quality/risk-of-bias appraisal is reported in the article. Each study was scored for reporting 16 set-and-setting sub-domains; the Methods states that no data synthesis was planned.
results.corrected_locator: Abstract (p. 1: 27 articles, 25 studies, 13 randomized/12 open-label, 763 participants); Materials and methods > Data source and research strategy and Eligibility criteria (p. 2); Outcome definition and data extraction (pp. 2–3, especially the final paragraph on p. 3); Data extraction (p. 4); Results > Study selection and Characteristics of the studies, first and second paragraphs (p. 4); Table 1, all rows (pp. 5–6). Absence of reported review protocol/registration and formal trial appraisal checked in the article text, especially the complete Methods, pp. 2–4.

results.corrected_extracted: In a systematic review reporting 25 studies of classic psychedelics for psychiatric disorders (studies treating substance use disorders excluded; searches updated on 6 December 2023), the Results text reports 16 studies playing a predefined music selection through headphones. Table 3, however, describes Carhart-Harris et al. (2016), one of those entries, with high-quality stereo speakers, von Rotz et al. (2023) with headphones or speakers, and headphones as optional in Peck et al. (2023) and Sloshower et al. (2023). The Results describes one study, Holze et al. (2023), alternating music and silence without headphones. Table 3 explicitly describes two studies with no music: dos Santos et al. (2021), where music and movies were not allowed, and D'Souza et al. (2022), with no music or decoration. The Results text reports 11 studies recommending an eye mask throughout; Table 3 describes eye-shades as optional in Peck and Sloshower. The Discussion states that no studies compared psychedelic efficacy in different sets and settings, and cites Kaelen et al. (2018) as specifically investigating the relationship between subjective music experience and psychedelic experience. These are descriptions and conclusions reported by the review, rather than primary-trial procedures independently checked here.

(2023) rows (p. 14); Discussion, fourth and fifth paragraphs, beginning “The fact that a therapeutic effect...” and “An important dimension...” (p. 17).
